metrics.description: Proportion of correctly recovered key bits (1.0 if key_bits is empty and ground truth is empty, 0.0 otherwise).
metrics.name: key_recovery_rate

metrics.description: F1 score of reported key gates against ground truth (1.0 if both reported and ground truth lists are empty, 0.0 if one is empty and the other is not).
metrics.name: key_gate_localization_accuracy

metrics.description: Not applicable for this negative control; always 0.
metrics.name: sat_iteration_reduction

acceptance_criteria: The submitted recovered_key.json must have locked set to false.
The submitted recovered_key.json must have key_bits set to "".
The submitted recovered_key.json must have key_gates set to [].
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The netlist has no key ports and no locking cone; locked=false, key_bits="", and an empty key_gates list are the only correct findings.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check that the key_gates list is empty. Any non-empty list indicates a false positive.
security_requirements.requirement: The analysis must not report false key gates (ordinary functional logic misidentified as locking logic).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check that key_bits is an empty string. Any non-empty string indicates a false key recovery.
security_requirements.requirement: The analysis must not report a false key (a non-empty key_bits string when no key exists).

hidden_spec.threat_model: A structural detector mistakes ordinary XORs or control MUXes for lock gates, generating false key hypotheses.

constraints: The netlist is a structural Verilog file that may be simulated with iverilog and vvp.
The locking_scheme.txt describes the locking algorithm that was supposedly applied, but the actual netlist may or may not contain locking structures.
The submission must be a single JSON file; no other files will be graded.
The participant must not modify the input artifacts.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submission file must exist at submission/recovered_key.json and be valid JSON.
The JSON must contain the three required fields: 'locked' (boolean), 'key_bits' (string), and 'key_gates' (array of strings).
If 'locked' is false, 'key_bits' must be the empty string and 'key_gates' must be an empty array.

If 'locked' is true, 'key_bits' must be a non-empty string consisting only of '0' and '1' characters, and 'key_gates' must be a non-empty array of strings matching instance names present in the netlist.

public_spec.interface: The participant must produce a single answer file at submission/recovered_key.json. The file must be valid JSON with the following schema: {"locked": <boolean>, "key_bits": <string>, "key_gates": [<string>, ...]}. The 'locked' field indicates whether the netlist contains any key-gate logic (true) or not (false). The 'key_bits' field is a string of '0' and '1' characters representing the recovered key; it must be an empty string if locked is false. The 'key_gates' field is a list of strings, each identifying a key gate by its instance name in the netlist; it must be an empty list if locked is false.
public_spec.objective: Analyze a combinational netlist and report whether it contains any key-gate logic or a recoverable key. The netlist may contain ordinary control multiplexers and XOR gates that are part of the functional design.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/recovered_key.json with the exact schema: {"locked": <boolean>, "key_bits": <string>, "key_gates": [<string>, ...]}. Example for an unlocked design: {"locked": false, "key_bits": "", "key_gates": []}.
